title: Compact Cost Explorer: keyboard landmarks, locale-aware number condensation, and contrast token audit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Make the Cost Explorer compact view fully accessible and internationalization-ready while preserving dense information density for power users. This ticket covers three tightly coupled tasks: (1) introduce semantic keyboard landmarks and a lightweight skip-to-controls affordance for the compact layout, (2) implement locale-aware condensed number formatting (compact numbers like 1.2K/1,2K depending on locale) with clear aria-label fallbacks that expose exact values, and (3) run a contrast token audit for compact badges and sparklines to ensure WCAG AA compliance at small sizes.

Context: The compact mode was introduced to help customers scan many routes/models/targets at once. Engineering shipping the compact CSS and virtualization has created new a11y regressions: keyboard focus order is flattened into a DOM-optimized structure, compact numeric strings drop precision for display, and the tiny cost badges + muted sparkline colors fall below recommended contrast on some themes and locales (esp. Arabic numerals with different grouping separators).

Deliverables:
- Annotated prototype (Figma) showing keyboard landmarks (role="navigation" for filter toolbar, role="list" for row container, skip link at top) and explicit focus styles in compact density. Prototype includes detailed touchpoints for screen reader flow and voiceover heuristics.
- Locale-aware display rules: map between Intl.NumberFormat short/compact displays and aria-label full-value fallbacks; examples for en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, es-ES, and ar-SA.
- Contrast token proposals: 3 replacement tokens for compact badges and 2 for sparklines with hex values and contrast ratios measured against background tokens. Include alternate token set for high-contrast mode.
- Test plan and checklist: automated axe runs per locale, manual VoiceOver/JAWS sweep for row focus, keyboard-only navigation walkthrough, and visual regression snapshots for dark/light/high-contrast themes.

Constraints and non-goals: This work is surface-level UX and token recommendations; it does not change backend aggregation or change caching/formatting at the server. Where possible we prefer localized formatting at the client using Intl.NumberFormat with fallback strings from the API only if client cannot compute the requested display.

Acceptance criteria:
- All compact-mode interactive elements reachable via keyboard in a predictable order with a documented DOM landmark structure.
- Compact numeric displays show locale-appropriate compact strings visually, with aria-labels exposing precise numeric values (e.g., "$1,234.56" and for fr-FR "1,234,56 $" aria-label still reads full precision and currency).
- Contrast ratios for badges and sparklines meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for small text/icons) across light/dark themes, or alternate token set enabled via high-contrast mode.
- Prototype reviewed and signed off by ENG and PM; accessibility test plan executed and first-pass issues triaged.
comments: 2026-02-06 - Aisha Patel: Initial working prototype uploaded. Included three compact rows with keyboard flow annotations and suggested token values. Figured a skip-to-controls anchor that moves to the filter toolbar and then the row list.

2026-02-12 - Miguel Santos: Engineering reviewed the prototype. Concern: virtualization changes DOM order which breaks sequential tab order. Suggested an agreed ARIA strategy where rows remain in logical DOM order and virtualization swaps only presentation nodes where feasible.

2026-02-15 - PM review (Lena Hoffman): Support for Intl.NumberFormat compact forms is approved, but we need explicit guidance for when to fall back to server-supplied localized strings for legacy browsers. PM requested examples for 3 locales including RTL.

2026-02-20 - Accessibility review (external consultant): Keyboard focus states are visible but contrast of focus ring on compact cards fails in dark theme at 2px stroke. Recommended increase to 3px or switch to an inset box-shadow approach for better visibility.

follow_up_tasks: ENG-9047 - Fix skiplink/focus conflict during scroll
ENG-9071 - Add Intl.NumberFormat polyfill check and server-fallback guidance
DES-32111 - Microcopy: aria-label patterns and examples for locale teams
notes_for_dev: Prefer client-side Intl.NumberFormat for compact displays; wrap with a helper that returns both compactString and fullPrecisionString.
Maintain DOM logical order even if virtualization reorders visual rows; use aria-posinset/aria-setsize if needed for large lists.
Expose a feature flag for gradual rollout and A/B validation of token changes.
design_decision_log: Use aria-label rather than title/tooltips for exposing full numeric precision to screen readers.
Adopt two token sets: default and high-contrast. Default tokens aim for 4.5:1 where possible; high-contrast tokens guaranteed >=7:1 for small UI elements.
Skiplink should land on the filter toolbar first, then focus the first interactive control; this preserves a predictable flow for assistive tech.
